title: [IELTS Trainer] - How patients evaluated health centre services
prompt: The table below shows how patients evaluated different services at three health centers. Summarise the information by selecting and reporting the main features, and make comparisons where relevant.

frame.name: Introduction
paragraphs: The table illustrates patient satisfaction ratings for five different service aspects across three health centres, namely Longston, Peveril, and Marchbank, on a scale from 1 (very poor) to 10 (excellent).

frame.name: Overview
paragraphs: Overall, Peveril Centre received the highest overall average rating, significantly outperforming Longston Centre. In addition, doctor's service was the most highly rated aspect across all three facilities, while booking appointments and response to concerns showed the greatest variation between centres.

frame.name: Body 1
paragraphs: First of all, regarding the most positively evaluated services, doctor's service received consistently high ratings across all three centres, with Peveril leading at 8.7, followed closely by Marchbank at 8.4 and Longston at 8.0, representing relatively minor differences of less than one point between facilities. Similarly, care of children was rated at 7.5 in Peveril, slightly higher than Marchbank's 7.3, while Longston recorded a notably lower score of 6.3, approximately 1.2 points below the highest-rated centre. Additionally, booking appointments showed considerable disparity, with Peveril achieving 9.1, compared to Marchbank's 7.8 and Longston's significantly lower 5.2, creating a gap of nearly 4 points between the best and worst performing centres in this category.

frame.name: Body 2
paragraphs: Secondly, as for the remaining aspects, pharmacy services received moderate ratings across all locations, with Peveril again performing best at 6.3, while Marchbank and Longston recorded 5.8 and 5.1, respectively. Moreover, response to concerns exhibited the most dramatic differences among all evaluated aspects, as Peveril scored an exceptional 9.6, considerably higher than Marchbank's 6.5 and Longston's notably poor 4.3, which represented the lowest rating recorded in the entire table.
